title: Humphrey teaching the grocery band and the spring cart
summary: Recalled story of the boys' band at the grocery and hauling Humphrey in the spring cart.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That was before my time, you see. I was around ten years old. I was just after my mother died. And I started waiting in that grocery place I was telling you about. And all of them used to gather there. The man we worked was a very good man. He always had a bunch of behind the very nice to cover people. And those boys got together and organized a band. And I think he paid for all the instruments, you know. That was twelve of them. I think he gave them all the instruments. They used to be at his place. But he used to keep it crowded all the time at the place, you see. And they used to rehearse a little there a couple of nights a week. And on Sunday, bless how we got to know Professor Jim Humphrey. See. And he used to come up there and teach George Brothers the same way. And I used to have to hold him when he was teaching them. A little old car that would come down and meet him. Take him back. See, and I still stayed there that band broke up. He was gone about six years before we started serving. And then I had to...
I hauled them the same way. I was joined then, I was in my 20s. I was over 20 when I started.
What kind of wagons did they have in those days when you'd bring them into town? Did they have surreys or carts?

No, they had a two-wheel spring cart, they called it. Two wheels? Two wheels, you know, with a spring on the spring. It wasn't what you call a dump cart, you know. No. The dump cart didn't have any spring, which was hard.
But this had springs on it.

But this had springs. We called it a spring cart, that's two wheels. And I used to haul them back and forth with that all the time. He helped me up and he talked to them on my way going back and forth. Even after I stopped getting listened for him, I used to meet him and he'd always have merit. A finer merit.
